title: Synthesis of Biocompatible Liquid Crystal Elastomer Foams as Cell Scaffolds for 3D Spatial Cell Cultures
protocol: Purify 27 g of 3-chloroperbenzoic acid by dissolving it in 35 mL of diethyl ether.
Wash the organic solution with 10 mL of buffer solution prepared using sodium phosphate monobasic and dibasic heptahydrate, adjusting pH to 7.4.
Repeat washing three times with 10 mL of buffer solution.
Add 3 g of sodium sulfate directly to the organic solution for drying.
Absorb water from the organic solution using sodium sulfate as a drying agent.
Filter the solution to remove the drying agent.
Concentrate the filtrate under reduced pressure using a rotary evaporator at 850 mbar and 40 °C.
Solubilize 18.5 g of purified 3-chloroperbenzoic acid in 150 mL of dry dichloromethane by stirring in an ultrasonic bath for 20 min.
Dissolve 13.1 g of 2-chlorocyclohexanone in 15 mL of dry dichloromethane using a magnetic stirrer under nitrogen gas.
Fit the separatory funnel containing the chloroperbenzoic acid solution to the two-neck flask with the 2-chlorocyclohexanone solution.
Flush the system with nitrogen gas.
Adjust the opening of the separatory funnel so that the chloroperbenzoic acid solution falls dropwise into the 2-chlorocyclohexanone solution (1 drop every other second).
Continue stirring the mixture under nitrogen gas for 96 h.
Cool the reaction mixture to -20 °C for 1 h to precipitate the m-chlorobenzoic acid byproduct.
Filter out the m-chlorobenzoic acid and wash the remaining solution with saturated solutions of sodium thiosulfate, sodium bicarbonate, and sodium chloride.
Remove the solvent under reduced pressure using a rotary evaporator at 850 mbar and 40 °C.
Purify the pale yellow, viscous liquid by distillation under reduced pressure at 2.3 Torr and 96 °C.
Monitor the success of the synthesis using the specified 1H NMR peaks.
Silanize a 20-mL ampoule by filling it with a 2% (v/v) solution of 1H,1H, 2H,2H-perfluorooctyltriethoxysilane in toluene and stirring for about 24 h.
Rinse the silanized ampoule with isopropyl alcohol.
Dry the rinsed ampoule by placing it in an oven at 140 °C for 30 min.
Add 3.64 g of distilled ε-caprolactone to the prepared ampoule.
Add 0.5 g of α-chloro-ε-caprolactone to the ampoule.
Add 0.25 mL of glycerol to the ampoule.
Mix the contents of the ampoule using a vortex for 1 min.
Add 4.90 g of D,L-lactide to the ampoule and purge it with nitrogen.
Place the ampoule in an oven at 120 °C to melt the D,L-lactide.
Reheat the mixture as needed until all contents are melted.
Mix again using a vortex to ensure proper mixing.
Add 66 µL of tin(II) 2-ethylhexanoate (Sn(Oc)t2) to the ampoule.
Vigorously mix one last time using the vortex.
Flush the final mixture with nitrogen.
Close the ampoule with a rubber stopper.
Connect a needle to a vacuum tube through the rubber stopper.
Turn on the vacuum and melt the long neck of the glass slowly without melting the rubber stopper.
Place the flame-sealed ampoule in a sand bath at 140 °C for 48 hours.
Remove the ampoule from the heat source and let it cool to room temperature.
Break the sealed mark on the ampoule and add 10 mL of dichloromethane to dissolve the liquid.
Transfer the solution to a separatory funnel.
Prepare a flask containing 100 mL of cold methanol at -78 °C.
Fix the separatory funnel on top of the prepared flask.
Adjust the separatory funnel so that about two drops fall every other second into the flask.
Collect the white precipitate by filtration using a paper filter.
Dry the collected precipitate in a vacuum oven between 50 and 60 °C.
Dissolve 5 g of SBC-αCl in 30 mL of dry N,N'-dimethylformamide under nitrogen.
Add 0.22 g of sodium azide and allow the reaction overnight at room temperature.
Remove N,N'-dimethylformamide under reduced pressure using a rotary evaporator at 11 mbar and 40 °C.
Dissolve the mixture in 30 mL of toluene.
Centrifuge the solution thrice at 2,800 x g for 15 min to remove salt formed.
Evaporate the toluene under reduced pressure using a rotary evaporator at 77 mbar and 40 °C.
Mix 3 g of 5-hexynoic acid with 130 mL of dichloromethane in a round-bottom flask.
Cool the mixture to 0 °C using an ice bath.
Mix 8.28 g of N,N'-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide, 10.3 g of cholesterol, and 0.2 g of 4-dimethylaminopyridine in another round-bottom flask.
Transfer the 5-hexynoic acid solution dropwise to the cholesterol mixture while maintaining a temperature of 0 °C.
Maintain the final mixture at 0 °C for 1 hour.
Allow the mixture to warm up to room temperature overnight.
Remove the dicyclohexylurea precipitate by filtration using a grade 415 paper filter and discard it.
Concentrate the filtrate under reduced pressure using a rotary evaporator at 850 mbar and 40 °C.
Dissolve the collected residue in 150 mL of hexane.
Dissolve 1 molar equivalent of SBC-αN3 (1.5 g) in 100 mL of freshly distilled tetrahydrofuran (THF).
Add 1.2 molar equivalent of cholesteryl 5-hexynoate (1.94 g), 0.1 molar equivalent of copper(I)iodide (0.06 g), and 0.1 molar equivalent of triethylamine (0.03 g).
Stir the mixture overnight at 35 °C under nitrogen.
Evaporate the solvent under reduced pressure using a rotary evaporator at 357 mbar and 40 °C.
Dissolve the residual mixture in 80 mL of dichloromethane.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 2,800 x g at room temperature to remove unreacted materials and side products.
Prepare a solution containing 10.8 g of 2-bis(4-hydroxy-cyclohexyl)propane in 52 mL of acetic acid.
Prepare a solution containing 11 g of chromium trioxide in 50 mL of acetic acid and 8 mL of distilled water.
Add the chromium trioxide solution dropwise to the solution prepared from step 6.1 while maintaining the mixture temperature between 17 and 20 °C; this process takes 2 h.
Allow the solution to stir for about 30 min after completing the addition.
Add 50 mL of 2-propanol.
Stir the solution overnight at room temperature.
Concentrate the dark purple solution under reduced pressure using a rotary evaporator at 137 mbar and 40 °C.
Add 300 mL of distilled water to precipitate; the precipitate should be light purple.
Filtrate the crude product using a grade 415 paper filter.
Wash the solid material with ~250 mL of distilled water or until the solid becomes white.
Dissolve the solid material in 15 mL of benzene at 40 °C and let it recrystallize at 25 °C.
Add 8.34 g of dry diketone dissolved in dry dichloromethane to the flask.
Add a solution containing 6.0 g of 3-chloroperbenzoic acid in 75 mL of dichloromethane to the flask.
Reflux the solution at 40 °C for 24 h.
Cool the reaction mixture to -20 °C for 10 min to precipitate the m-chlorobenzoic acid byproduct.
Remove m-chlorobenzoic acid by filtration (using a paper filter).
Concentrate the solution under reduced pressure.
Wash the viscose crude product with 200 mL of 2-heptanone.
Dry the precipitate under vacuum at 50 °C overnight.
Prepare three-arm elastomer mixture using 0.75 g of SBC-αCLC by adding 0.25 mL of HDI (or 0.45 mL of BCP) and 0.24 mL of distilled ε-caprolactone monomer.
Add 60 μL of Sn(Oct)2 to the mixture.
If using BCP, mix SBC-αCLC and BCP using a vortex and place in an oven at 140 °C until BCP fully melts and dissolves.
Once BCP is dissolved, take it out of the oven and add Sn(Oct)2 before mixing with a vortex.
Cut a 1 x 4 cm metal piece for a "sacrificial" nickel foam template.
Roll the metal from one short end to form an approximately 1 x 1 cm roll.
Place the rolled nickel foam in a glass vial or aluminum foil pack and pour the elastomer mixture over it to fully cover for 2 min.
Remove excess mixture with a Pasteur pipet and leave in an oven overnight at 80 °C.
Peel off aluminum foil or break the glass containing the foam.
Shave the elastomer around the metal foam using a razor blade to expose nickel metal.
Prepare 1 M iron(III)chloride (FeCl3) solution in 100 mL of water.
Place the foam in a flask and add 70 mL of FeCl3 solution, stirring for three days at room temperature.
Change the FeCl3 solution every day.
Before each change, stir the foam with ionized water for 0.5 h.
Sterilize the elastomer by washing it twice with 1 mL of 70% ethanol.
Perform UV irradiation for 10 min and wash with 1 mL of 70% ethanol.
Rinse the elastomer twice with 1 mL of sterile water and once with 1 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Place the elastomers in 24-well culture plates.
Prepare cell growth medium for SH-SY5Y containing 90% Dulbecco Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1% Penicillin-Streptomycin (Pen-Strep).
After counting the cells using a hematocytometer, prepare 1.5 x 10^5 SH-SY5Y cells suspended in 100 μL of growth medium.
Add the solution on top of the elastomers to form a drop.
Incubate the seeded elastomers at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 2 h to promote cell adhesion.
Add 0.5 mL of growth medium.
Incubate again at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Change the medium every other day after washing with 1 mL of PBS.
Fix the cells grown on elastomers with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 15 min.
Rinse with 3 mL of PBS three times for 5 min each.
Place the elastomer with the fixed cells in a culture dish with an attached coverslip.
Stain the fixed samples with 0.1% of 4',6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI) in 500 µL of PBS for 10 min.
Rinse twice with 1 mL of PBS for 5 min.
Image the elastomers using confocal microscopy with DAPI fluorescence, acquiring image stacks that span the sample.
